It was a common name in biblical times, particularly among the Jewish priestly class. One notable bearer of this name was Elazar, the son of Aaron, who was a high priest in the Tabernacle and later in the First Temple.

During the Middle Ages, the name Elazarus was also used as a variant of the name Lazarus, which comes from the Greek form of the Hebrew name Eliezer, meaning 'God is my help'. The New Testament tells the story of Lazarus of Bethany, who was raised from the dead by Jesus.
